title: R' Abba bar Yaakov bar Idi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: So he is listed in Seder HaDorot, citing the beginning of Terumot chapter 3. Hyman calls this an error: the passage reads ‘R' Ba; R' Yaakov bar Idi in the name of R' Yonatan.’ For Hyman, the plain meaning is that R' Ba reports in R' Yaakov bar Idi's name; this is clear.

notes.text: ר״פג means the beginning of chapter 3, not chapter 83. ופשט הפשיט is read contextually as “the plain meaning”; it does not name a careless copyist. The consulted Terumot paragraph actually has Ba bar Yaakov bar Idi, whereas Hyman quotes juxtaposed names and interprets a reporting chain. This remains a source question, with no genealogical correction adopted.

The saved whole Mechon-Mamre Terumot3:1 scalar matches Hyman’s unconnected Ba, Yaakov bar Idi, in Yonatan’s name; the whole Venice scalar instead reads Ba bar Yaakov bar Idi. Thus the old blanket conflict claim is superseded for Mechon-Mamre, but neither digital edition proves Hyman’s printed witness or SederHaDorot’s source. Hyman forcefully calls the filial reading an error and his reporting interpretation clear. ר״פג is beginning of chapter3, not83; ופשט הפשיט is contextual plain meaning, not a careless copyist. Full Rabbi titles in Venice do not determine the abbreviated separate-transmitter occurrences in Mechon-Mamre.

The Warsaw Seder HaDorot entry names Abba bar Yaakov bar Idi in Rabbi Yonatan’s name. Venice and Guggenheimer give the connected name in Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 3:1:6, whereas Mechon-Mamre places Ba and Yaakov bar Idi side by side in the Yonatan clause. The preceding clause cites Rabbi Yochanan. The juxtaposition is the basis of Hyman’s interpretation of the transmission.
